title: Biomarker guided assessment for clinical outcomes in acute kidney injury – a retrospective analysis of the BigpAK-2 trial
summary:
Approximately one in five patients develops temporary kidney damage after a major operation. This can lead to additional health problems, increase the risk of death, and may result in long-term kidney disease.

The BigpAK-2 study investigated whether a specific substance in the urine can help identify patients who are at increased risk of developing kidney damage after a major operation. The substance was measured in the urine shortly after the operation in order to assess this risk as early as possible.

The present analysis uses data that have already been collected to investigate whether complications after surgery occur more often in different groups of patients. Patients with and without kidney damage will be compared. Within each of these groups, patients with and without an increased-risk result from the urine test will also be compared. The results may help to identify patients at particularly high risk of further health problems at an early stage after major surgery in the future.

Inclusion criteria:
Data analysis of patients who underwent major surgery at Münster University Hospital between November 2020 and June 2024 and who gave their written consent to participate in the BigpAK-2 study and in whom the urinary biomarker [TIMP-2]*[IGFBP7]  was measured postoperatively.
